title: Where to Go Next: Enhancing Zero-Shot Capability for Cross-City Mobility Prediction

problem.claim: Deploying next-location prediction models in a new city requires substantial historical mobility data and costly retraining.

gap.claim: Existing methods are largely city-bound because their inputs and outputs use city-specific identifiers, causing performance to collapse when the city changes.

contributions.claim: ReLoX is a framework for zero-shot cross-city mobility prediction.
ReLoX combines an anchor-centered relative trajectory representation with a local egocentric image capturing nearby spatial relations and semantics.
ReLoX uses dual encoders and a gated hierarchical module to extract and fuse sequential and visual cues.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on large-scale mobility data across three cities report that ReLoX remains competitive for within-city prediction.
The authors report substantial gains under cross-city zero-shot protocols, where city-bound baselines largely fail.

narrative_sequence.summary: Next-location prediction supports personalized recommendations and demand forecasting.
New-city deployment is expensive because models require historical target-city mobility data and retraining.
Existing city-bound methods do not transfer effectively when the city changes.
ReLoX combines relative trajectory and local spatial-semantic representations with dual encoding and gated fusion.
The authors report competitive within-city results and substantial cross-city zero-shot gains across three cities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the mobility datasets, city identities, data sizes, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not report ablations, computational costs, or robustness across additional cities.
The abstract does not describe the target-city adaptation requirements beyond stating that zero-shot inference uses no target-city adaptation.
